critical_resolutions.CRITICAL-1_subgroup_size_32_typed_skip: RESOLVED. The subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip is now MANDATED on all three GPU dispatch paths, exactly mirroring the AT-1510 precedent (dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231, which I verified reads `if ctx.subgroup_size() != 32 { eprintln!(... wave64 guard ...); return; }`): (a) AT-1743 description (architect line 128) carries the guard IN ADDITION to the CoopMatUnsupported/Lavapipe skip; (b) AT-1744 (line 135) carries it; (c) AT-1750/resident_matmul_msg.rs (line 149 + coder_handoff line 179) carries it BEFORE allocation/dispatch. The false 'still correct on any wave width' / 'degrade to single-subgroup' claims are REMOVED and REPLACED with honest, explicit failure-mode text in ALL FOUR loci: EC-2 (line 158: 'HARD PRECONDITION, TYPED-SKIPPED (NOT silently correct)'), technical_spec PART-B (line 103: '**HARD PRECONDITION — subgroup_size MUST be 32 (typed-skipped otherwise, NOT silently correct)**'), design_md_additions PART-B (line 184), and the coder_handoff_notes (line 176, 'DO NOT claim portability/graceful-degrade in any comment'). The two failure modes are stated EXPLICITLY and correctly in every locus: wave64 (sg_id=local_x/64=0 for all 64 threads => only ONE subgroup runs => C cols [block_col*64+32..+64) NEVER written => HALF of C garbage; explicitly NOT a degrade-to-single-subgroup because the MSG grid is 64-col-per-WG) and SIMD16 (sg_id in {0,1,2,3} => B-read offset sg_id*32 in {64,96} OOB of the 64-wide b_tile + C col base block_col*64+{64,96} writes into the NEXT workgroup's region => cross-workgroup overwrite race). The .axc header (files_to_create line 20 + coder_handoff lines 176/178) MUST document the sg_size==32 precondition.
critical_resolutions.CRITICAL-2_bit_exact_by_construction: RESOLVED. The design now states bit-exactness is GUARANTEED BY CONSTRUCTION by the emitted workgroup-scope OpControlBarrier (execution scope Workgroup=2, memory semantics 0x108 = AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory; emit_workgroup_barrier subgroup.rs:285-301, unit-tested subgroup.rs:476), explicitly NOT merely by AT-1743 passing (which on NVIDIA could pass via near-lockstep luck masking a weaker barrier). This is stated in technical_spec ('**BIT-EXACTNESS IS GUARANTEED BY CONSTRUCTION**', line 103), EC-3 (line 159), correctness_oracle (line 155), OQ-2 (line 167), AT-1743 description (line 128), and design_md_additions (line 184). The justification that there is NO subgroup-scope barrier emission path to weaken it is carried in every locus. The loop-bottom WAR barrier coverage (K>16 only; AT-1743 K=32 => 2 K-blocks once, AT-1744 K=48 => 3 K-blocks twice) is now stated.

warning_resolutions.staging_coverage_assert: RESOLVED. AT-1745 (line 142) now asserts a_block_size % wg_threads == 0 AND b_block_size % wg_threads == 0 (512%64==0 -> 8 iters; 1024%64==0 -> 16 iters) AND shared_memory_bytes == 3072 <= 16384. The STAGING-COVERAGE INVARIANT is also stated in technical_spec (line 103). This closes the AT-1620 staging-bug class for the shipped @strategy assignment.
warning_resolutions.body_scanner_coverage: RESOLVED. coder_handoff (line 175), emit.rs change (line 61), and a revision_changelog entry require body_uses_local_invocation_id to be a FULL traversal mirroring body_uses_gid (emit.rs:457-529), recursing into LOOP-BOUND expressions, SHARED-WRITE INDEX expressions, nested binops, AND the sg_id numerator. warning_resolutions.non_symmetric_fixture: RESOLVED/RETAINED. AT-1743/1744 (lines 128/135) and coder_handoff (line 180) retain the M3.3c non-symmetric integer-f16 fixture (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}) with an explicit 'do NOT substitute a symmetric one' directive, justified by the NEW 64-wide stride-64 b_tile (a swapped sg_id offset or wrong stride must yield max_diff != 0).

new_hole_check.guard_is_test_bench_side_not_runtime_pre: ACCEPTABLE for M3.3d's shipped scope, honestly bounded. The .axc kernel itself carries NO runtime subgroup-size predication; the correctness discipline is the test/bench-side typed-skip. This leaves NO real hole for the SHIPPED scope because the ONLY dispatch paths that ever run matmul_msg_coopmat.axc are AT-1743, AT-1744, and AT-1750 — ALL THREE now carry the subgroup_size()==32 guard. There is no other code path that dispatches this kernel. The residual risk (single-vendor NVIDIA wave32 validation; guard is discipline rather than kernel-enforced) is honestly bounded in EC-2 (line 158), OQ-2 (line 167), and vendor_concerns of r0; the alternative kernel-runtime enforcement (requiredSubgroupSize=32 via VK_EXT_subgroup_size_control at pipeline creation) is explicitly named and deferred out of M3.3d scope. This is the same discipline already shipped and accepted for AT-1510 (matmul_tile).
new_hole_check.subgroup_size_zero_props_unavailable: NO HOLE. context.rs:709 subgroup_size() returns 0 when VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan11Properties is unavailable. 0 != 32, so the `!= 32` guard correctly typed-skips in that degenerate case too (no dispatch of the miscomputing kernel).

No codegen change beyond the already-correct local_invocation_id builtin (which I confirmed sound in r0). No new annotation, no new capability (spirv_capabilities_added_this_milestone == []), no new SPIR-V op. self_check flags (subgroup_size_32_typed_skip_mandated_on_AT_1743_1744_1750, ec2_honest_no_false_portability_claim, barrier_bit_exact_guaranteed_by_construction, staging_coverage_invariant_asserted_in_AT_1745, body_scanner_full_traversal_specified, no_gid_emit_shortcut_copied_to_local_invocation_id, non_symmetric_fixture_for_64wide_b_tile_retained) are all true and match the spec body.

CRITICAL-1: the subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip is now MANDATED on AT-1743, AT-1744, and AT-1750 (every dispatch path that runs matmul_msg_coopmat.axc), mirroring the verified AT-1510 precedent (dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231) using the verified accessor (context.rs:709); the false 'still correct on any wave width' claim is removed from EC-2, technical_spec PART-B, design_md_additions, and coder_handoff, and replaced with honest, explicit failure-mode text (wave64: sg_id=0 => only one subgroup runs => half of C never written; SIMD16: sg_id*32 OOB shared read + cross-workgroup C overwrite).
